(2025). Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis. arXiv.
creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
description: Video-MME is a comprehensive multimodal evaluation benchmark for video analysis by multimodal large language models. It contains 900 videos across 6 visual domains and 30 categories, with 2,700 expert-annotated multiple-choice question-answer pairs, and includes associated subtitles and audio for many videos.
name: Video-MME
publisher: Nanjing University, XMU, HKU, PKU, CUHK, ECNU, CASIA, State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were recruited with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify clarity, answerability, logical consistency of options, and correctness of the designated answer. The authors also provided text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro and filtered out QA pairs answerable from text alone; Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in this text-only setup.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: After collecting raw videos, annotators thoroughly viewed each entire video and iteratively created three relevant multiple-choice questions, each with four candidate options, for a total of 2,700 QA pairs. Questions were designed to be closely tied to video content so they could not be answered accurately without referencing the video.
rai:dataBiases: To reduce bias from answering questions using textual priors alone, the authors filtered out QA pairs that Gemini 1.5 Pro could answer from the text-only questions without viewing the video, and returned such questions to annotators for revision.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed in three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Raw videos were sourced from YouTube using a domain hierarchy covering 6 key domains and 30 fine-grained categories, with short, medium, and long durations; corresponding subtitles and audio were also obtained when available.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Subtitles were not available for all videos: the dataset includes 744 videos with subtitles out of 900 total videos, while all 900 videos have audio.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consist of YouTube videos collected across 6 domains and 30 categories, along with corresponding meta-information such as subtitles when provided and audio tracks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that long-form video understanding remains challenging, with model performance declining as video duration increases. It also notes that the availability of complex temporal reasoning datasets is limited and that subtitle quality may affect results in some categories such as multilingual videos.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were organized into short, medium, and long duration groups. For evaluation with subtitles, subtitles corresponding to sampled video-frame timestamps were selected to ensure synchronization between visual and textual inputs.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models on video understanding, including perception, reasoning, information synthesis, temporal understanding, and multimodal understanding with frames, subtitles, and audio.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used in quality review to test whether questions could be answered from text-only questions; QA pairs that could be answered without the video were filtered out and revised.
